title: The Cost of Convenience
sentences: Almost everything I use now arrives without any effort on my part.
Food, films and conversation are all a single tap away.
It took me years to notice what that convenience quietly removed.
Waiting used to create small pockets of unstructured thought.
Those pockets have been filled in, one by one, by something more entertaining.
I am not convinced that the exchange has been in my favour.
The argument against this is obvious and reasonable enough.
Nobody genuinely misses standing in a queue at a bank.
But convenience is rarely offered to us as a choice between equals.
It arrives already installed, and the alternative has to be reconstructed deliberately.
